$comment: Paths the PUBLICATION CUT removes from this suite, declared ONCE so the cut
and the guards read the same list instead of two that drift.
Why a declaration and not a hand-edit at cut time: the last cut dropped four
script directories by hand, and the guards that exempt files inside them had
no way to tell 'deliberately not in this cut' from 'exemption has gone stale'.
An exempt file that is absent AND listed here is the former; absent and NOT
listed here stays a failure, so the ratchet keeps its teeth in both trees.
What earns a place here: scripts that execute WRITES against a live estate,
and internal measurement rigs that answer questions about our lab rather than
about this software. Everything else ships.
An entry ending in '/' is a directory prefix; anything else is an exact path.
Paths are POSIX and relative to the suite root (the directory holding
package.json), which is also the publication tree's ROOT.
$includeComment: Paths OUTSIDE the suite subtree that the cut must nonetheless ship, because
the flat layout puts them at the tree root.
.github/ holds ci.yml, which was moved to the repository ROOT last session —
GitHub Actions reads workflows only from there. The suite's own
.github/workflows/ is consequently EMPTY, so a cut that exported only the
subtree shipped with no CI at all and nobody would have noticed until the
V11-AUDIT.md is required by v11-audit-covers-every-call-site, whose message
puts it best: a tree that ships the calls must ship the audit.
